questions.question: Who among the following wrote two books on the history and dance structure of Mohiniyattam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma **was an epoch-making Mohiniyattam dance use from Kerala in southern India.
 
• A native of **Thirunavaya** in the **Malappuram** district of the state, she was instrumental in resurrecting Mohiniyattam from a dismal, near-extinct state into a mainstream Indian classical dance, rendering it formal structure and ornamentation.
 
• The two books Kalyanikutty Amma has authored, "**Mohiniyattam - History and Dance Structure**" is considered as elaborate and only authentic documentation of Mohiniyattam.
 
• **Kalyanikutty Amma** passed the art of Mohiniyattam beyond **India**.
 
• The first Russian dancer, **Mohiniyattam**, was **Milana Severskaya**.
 
• In 1997,** Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma** blessed her on the continuation of the **Mohiniyattam** tradition.
 
• **Milana Severskaya** created in St. Petersburg, Russia the first outside India school of education for Mohiniattam.
 
• She founded the Natya Theater, where you can see the choreography of **Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma **in the play, dedicated to her memory.
 
• **Milana Siverskaya** has released a film dedicated to the memory of the **guru Kalyanikutty Amma** in which one can see how the guru taught dance in deep old age.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dr. Kalamandalam** **Radhika** is an Indian classical dancer, choreographer, research scholar, teacher, writer, and philanthropist. She was the first non-resident Keralite to win the Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Akademi award for **Mohiniyattam**. She learned Kuchipudi, Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, and other dance forms.
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is an Indian classical dance form that developed and remained popular in the state of **Kerala**. 
 
• **Thiruvananthapuram **(or Trivandrum) is the capital of the southern Indian state of Kerala.

questions.question: In which year will India host the ICC Champions Trophy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2029**__.**​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India** will host the ICC Men's Champions Trophy in **October** **2029**. 
 
• India will host **three** ICC events in the **2024-31 cycle**. 
 
• The **BCCI** will host the **2026 T20 World Cup **(with Sri Lanka), **the 2029 Champions Trophy** as well as the **2031 ODI World Cup** (with Bangladesh).
 
• **Pakistan **will be hosting the **2025 ICC Men's Champions Trophy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** ICC Champions Trophy** is a **One-Day International** (ODI) cricket tournament organised by the **International Cricket Council**.
 
• The** 2013** tournament was intended to be the **final edition** of the Champions Trophy, but it was extended to **2017** due to its widespread popularity.
 
• In **2018**, the ICC decided to replace the tournament with the** World Twenty20 championship** to be held every two years, and no Champions Trophy was contested in 2021.
 
• However, as part of the **2021** Future Tour Programme, the event was reinstated for the **2025** cycle onwards.
 
• In November 2021, the ICC confirmed the tournament would next take place in **2025** in **Pakistan**, with **India** hosting the tournament in **2029**.

questions.question: The first train inaugurated in 1853 was between which two stations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mumbai and Thane__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The first train on the Indian sub-continent ran from** Bori Bunder in Mumbai to Thane **at 3.30 pm on **April 16, 1853.** 
 
• The 14-carriage train carried **400 guests** and covered a distance of **34 km**. 
 
• The inaugural journey received a salute of **21 guns**.
 
• Today, Indian Railways runs around **11,000 trains daily**, of which **7,000** are passenger trains.
 
• The first Railway Workshop was established at** Jamalpur, near Munger, Bihar, in 1862.**
 
• It gradually became one of the major industrial units of India, with** iron and steel foundries, rolling mills** **and more.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Railways** is a statutory body under the ownership of the Ministry of Railways, Government of India that operates India's national railway system. 
 
• It manages the fourth largest national railway system in the world by size, with a total route length of **67,956 km** as of 31 March 2022.
 
• Indian Railways runs a total of 23,000+ trains daily of which 13,000+ are passenger services and 9,200+ services are freight.
 
• The Railway Minister of India currently is Ashwini Vaishnaw. Piyush Goyal was the minister before that.

questions.question: What is the domestic income if national income is ₹10,000 crore and net factor income from abroad is ₹2,000 crore?

__
 
• Domestic income (NDPFC) is the net money value of all the final goods and services produced within the domestic territory of a country during a period of one year**.
 
• **many non-residential companies and foreign banks operate within the domestic (economic) territory of India**. 
 
• Income generated by them is included in India's domestic income. Thus domestic income is a territorial concept since it is defined with reference to the domestic territory.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Income generated by them is included in India's domestic income. Thus domestic income is a territorial concept since it is defined with reference to domestic territory

questions.question: The bodies of the animals of phylum Platyhelminthes show _______ grade organisation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**tissue-organ**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A tissue organ is** an organ that lies between tissue and an organ system**. Tissues are formed from the same type of cells to act together in a function.
 
• Tissues of different types combine to form an organ that has a specific function. ​
 
• **Characteristics of phylum Platyhelminthes are:**​
 
 
• Their body is dorsoventrally flattened.
 
• They exhibit bilateral symmetry.
 
• Also, they are triploblastic, with three germ layers.
 
• They do not have a body cavity and are acoelomate.
 
• The body is soft and unsegmented.
 
• They are mostly parasitic with a few free-living.
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Protoplasm** is **the cytoplasm and nucleus of a cell**.

 
 
• The term was first defined in 1835 as the ground substance of living material and, hence, responsible for all living processes.
 
 
 
• ​An organelle or Cellular 
 
 
• it is **a membrane-bound structure found within a cell** Just like cells have membranes to hold everything in, these mini-organs are also bound in a double layer of phospholipids to insulate their little compartments within the larger cells.
 
 
 
• **Cell-Tissue** is **a group of cells that have similar structures and that function together as a unit**.
 
 
• Primary types of body tissues include epithelial, connective, muscular, and nervous tissues.

questions.question: Which group was given the name ‘paraffins’ earlier?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Alkanes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alkanes group was given the name ‘paraffin’.**
 
• Paraffins, also known as alkanes, are saturated compounds that have the general formula** CnH₂ₙ₊₂**, where n is the number of carbon atoms. 
 
• The simplest alkane is methane **(CH₄)**, which is also represented as** C₁**.
 
• Alkanes are called paraffin because they have a little affinity towards a general reagent. In other words, alkanes are inert substances. 
 
• Paraffin wax was first produced commercially in 1867, less than 10 years after the first petroleum well was drilled.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In organic chemistry, an aldehyde is an organic compound containing a functional group with the structure **R−CH=O.**
 
• The common names of aldehydes are taken from the names of the corresponding carboxylic acids: formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, and so on
 
• Alcohol is an organic compound with a** hydroxyl (OH)** functional group on an aliphatic carbon atom.
 
• OH is the functional group of all alcohols, we often represent alcohols by the general formula** ROH,** where R is an alkyl group.
 
• The word acid is derived from the Latin acidus/acēre, meaning** 'sour'.**
 
• There are two basic types of acids organic and inorganic acids. Inorganic acids are sometimes referred to as mineral acids.
